child.name: Elsie
child.hair: wavy ginger hair to her shoulders

setting.culture: A family in St Ives, Cornwall, on the English seaside - a stone harbour with a curved granite pier, small moored fishing boats, whitewashed cottages with grey slate roofs climbing the hill, seagulls, golden sand at low tide; smooth cobbled lanes.

object_placements.object: Paper boat, including the original white sheet and all folded stages

data.title: Elsie and the Paper Boat

premise.hero_want: Elsie wants to make a paper boat and sail it in a rock pool.
premise.problem: The boat tips to one side when Elsie tests it.
premise.mechanism: Elsie uses the familiar folds of a traditional paper boat. Its open base lets it float.
premise.resolution: Elsie lifts the boat out, pats its base flat and sails it again.

key_objects.name: Paper boat
key_objects.description: One white rectangular sheet that becomes a traditional folded paper boat with a red sail painted on one side.

key_objects.name: Red paint pot
key_objects.description: A small, open pot of red finger paint.

cast.appearance: Warm brown skin and dark brown curly hair in hair exactly as in her reference image. She wears a yellow long-sleeved top, blue trousers and red wellington boots. Her knees and shoulders are covered. Her eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: Elsie has paper and red paint. “I want to make a boat,” she said.
pages.scene: At low tide in St Ives harbour, Elsie sits on the golden sand beside a shallow rock pool. She holds one flat, white rectangular sheet. The small red paint pot is beside her. The curved granite pier and a few moored fishing boats are in the background. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: She bends the paper end to end. She bends each top tip in.
pages.scene: In the same spot, Elsie presses the two short ends of the white sheet together, then bends the two top corners towards the centre. The red paint pot stays beside her. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: She bends the flaps up. She tugs the gap wide.
pages.scene: Elsie bends the two lower flaps up to make the familiar paper hat shape. She opens the gap underneath and flattens it into a diamond. Keep the red paint pot beside her. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: She bends the tips up. She tugs the gap wide.
pages.scene: Elsie bends the lower tips of the paper diamond upwards. She opens the new gap and flattens the paper into a smaller diamond. Whitewashed cottages with grey slate roofs climb the hill behind the harbour. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: She pulls the top tips out. The paper is a boat!
pages.scene: Elsie pulls the two top points apart. The sheet opens into a traditional paper boat with a wide, flat base. She smiles at it. The red paint pot remains beside her. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: Elsie paints a red sail on the side. She must wait.
pages.scene: Elsie uses one fingertip to paint a simple red triangular sail on one side of the white paper boat. The boat rests on the sand while the paint dries. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: The boat sails in a rock pool. No! It tips to one side.
pages.scene: Elsie kneels at the same shallow rock pool. The dry white boat with its red painted sail floats, then leans sharply to one side. Elsie notices at once and reaches towards it. A seagull is far off on the curved granite pier. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

pages.text: Elsie lifts it out and pats the base flat. The boat sails on.
pages.scene: Elsie pats the base of the paper boat flat, then sets it back in the rock pool. It floats upright with the red sail facing her. Elsie beams. The harbour, small fishing boats and hillside cottages remain behind her. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

data.cover_brief: Elsie kneels on the golden sand beside a clear rock pool at low tide. Her finished traditional white paper boat floats upright, with the red painted sail visible. Behind her are St Ives’ curved granite pier, small moored fishing boats and whitewashed cottages with grey slate roofs climbing the hill. Keep the scene uncluttered and warm. Elsie wears her yellow long-sleeved top, blue trousers and red wellington boots. Her eyes are solid black filled ovals.

data.cold_read: A clear, warm build story at exemplar level. Elsie drives every stage, tests what she has made, notices the problem and fixes it herself. The paper boat is familiar and drawable. The story stays in one location with two key objects, no adult and one simple mechanism. The phonics contract and read_words pattern are met.

issues.detail: “She bends the paper end to end” sounds like an instruction rather than something a young child would naturally say. It has been changed to “She bends the paper so the ends meet.”

pages.carries_forward: The completed white boat keeps its narrow pinched base; the waiting red paint pot is used next.

pages.brief: Medium-close profile composed for possible cover use. Elsie is on the left with her face clear and a soft, proud smile. The white paper boat rests on dry golden sand on the right. Its base remains narrow and slightly pinched. Elsie has painted one simple red triangle on its visible side with her fingertip. She holds her red-tipped finger away while the wet paint dries. The open red paint pot is beside the boat, and the nearby rock pool is visible beyond. Her eyes are solid black filled ovals.

required_visible_states.assertion: It has the same narrow pinched base and one newly painted wet red triangle on its side.
The same open pot is beside the boat and Elsie’s fingertip has matching red paint.
Her clear, happy face and fixed appearance match earlier pages.

forbidden_visible_states.assertion: It is not yet in the water.
It is painted directly on the paper, not attached as a separate sail or mast.

pages.carries_forward: The red triangle dries in the same position; the narrow pinched base remains for the first water test.

pages.brief: Low water-level close shot. The same white paper boat dominates the shallow rock pool. Its narrow, pinched base makes it lean sharply towards one side. That lower paper edge touches the water and visibly darkens with damp. The red painted triangle is dry and unchanged. In the upper background, part of Elsie’s concerned face and one hand reach safely from the sand. Her visible eyes are solid black filled ovals.

required_visible_states.assertion: Its narrow pinched base is visibly connected to its sharp lean in the water.
The dipped lower edge is darker where water has soaked into it.
The dry painted triangle remains on the same side.
She remains on dry sand and reaches towards the boat.

forbidden_visible_states.assertion: It is not sunk, torn or replaced.

pages.carries_forward: Elsie lifts out this same boat; its damp lower edge remains while she broadens and flattens the pinched base.

pages.brief: Tight payoff reaction shot. Elsie’s delighted face and upper body fill the left side as she looks down at the same boat floating upright in the lower foreground. Its corrected base is visibly broad and flat. The red painted sail still faces her, and a faint darker damp line remains along the lower paper edge from page 7. The curved granite pier and hillside cottages are soft in the background. Elsie’s eyes are solid black filled ovals.

required_visible_states.assertion: Its broadened flat base is visibly connected to its upright position in the water.
A faint damp line remains along the lower edge from the failed test.
The same red painted triangle remains on the same side.
Her fixed appearance and large delighted reaction are clear.

forbidden_visible_states.assertion: It must not appear pristine, dry, newly replaced or fitted with extra parts.

pages.carries_forward: Final state: the original paper boat floats upright with its corrected flat base, persistent red sail and faint damp edge.
